content.text: {"headline":"Approve R2 (late break shift on both queues + outage message, callback and chat deflection) for ₹603. It is the best available plan at 58.9% for 10:45-12:45, short of the 80% target, so involve the duty manager now.","why":"The spike comes from the UPI switch outage (INC-20261006-6998), not from staffing. Payments calls ran +90% at 10:30 (213 vs 111.9 forecast), driven by upi_payment_failed calls at 2.56x normal. We are at plan with 42 of 43 agents, so the fix is to cut demand and keep agents on the phones. R2 plays the outage IVR message, offers callbacks and pushes 20% of status enquiries to chat. It also cancels payments coaching 11:00-12:00 and moves all breaks due 11:45-12:30 back 45 minutes. Predicted results for 10:45-12:45: service level 58.9% (payments 48.4%, general 76.0%) and abandons 10.8%. With no action, service level would be 29.4% with 22.2% abandons. Rest of day is 79.9%. No plan reaches 80%. Overtime is off the table today, with no budget.","trade_offs":["R1 costs the same ₹603 but only delays payments breaks. It predicts 55.7% (general 70.4%), so R2 gains about 3 points by also shifting general-queue breaks, with general still at 76.0%.","P3 and P4 cost ₹555, only ₹48 less, but predict 49.2% and 48.4% because their break delays fall inside the peak.","P2 is the cheapest meaningful option at ₹75 but reaches only 45.1% with 15.1% abandons.","P1 is free but makes things worse (26.6%) than doing nothing."],"watch":"Escalate to the duty manager: even the best compliant plan is predicted at 59% for 10:45-12:45, below the 70% escalation line (ESC-02). Payments will stay at about 48% while the UPI incident is open. Track the incident status, the payments abandon rate and general-queue service level after the 11:45 break shift. Be ready to extend or remove the IVR outage message as soon as UPI recovers."}
